title: A four-edge obstruction to submodular separation of quadratic Boolean monomial images: a counterexample to Brakensiek-Gopi-Guruswami Conjecture 3.33 (arXiv:1902.04740; ECCC TR19-013)
beyond_target: accepted after the campaign target of 40 was reached (additional result #44 toward 60)
exact_endpoint: Separation.source_existence_refuted : ¬ Separation.SeparationExistence, where SeparationExistence := for all d r with r <= d there is f : Point d -> Z that is submodular on allowed points (union/intersection), <= -1 on every monomial image phi r X (filtered powerset, including the empty monomial) and >= 0 on every allowed non-image point; Conjecture 3.33 (which also asks for poly(n)-time evaluation) implies SeparationExistence
scope: Conjecture 3.33 is false at (r,d) = (2,5): no integer- (indeed real-) valued submodular function on {0,1}^16 is negative exactly on the degree-2 monomial image of {0,1}^5.
source_targets: Brakensiek-Gopi-Guruswami arXiv:1902.04740v1 / ECCC TR19-013 Conjecture 3.33 (SIAM J. Comput. 51(3) (2022) 577-626 as listed by the authors)

substantive_reason: It refutes, at the interior parameter (r,d)=(2,5), the universal submodular-separation conjecture on which the source's proposed SUBMOD-MIN-MOD_M hardness reduction (Proposition 3.34, Corollary 3.35) depends. The impossibility is witnessed by an explicit four-edge dependency cycle (an application of the Elbracht-Kneip-Teegen criterion) and independently by a 13-row symmetric certificate. Significance is modest; the complexity of modular submodular minimization is not decided.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; not worldwide priority; no new general obstruction claimed
trust_limits: the poly-time clause is not formalized (refuting bare existence suffices)
